verdict: Steel Dynamics nearly doubled operating income to $1.0B as steel prices rose, scrap costs fell and shipments hit a record 3.8 million tons — sales jumped 35% to $6.5B.

kpis.label: Steel operating income
kpis.note: up 43% from the prior quarter, on record shipments and wider metal spreads

kpis.label: Cash flow from operations
kpis.note: capital spending was $150M in the quarter — money spent on buildings and equipment

segments.name: Steel operations
segments.note: Making and selling steel — record shipments of 3.8 million tons and an average external selling price of $1,400 per ton drove the jump.

segments.name: Other
segments.note: Smaller businesses outside the four main platforms, as classified in the company's supplemental sales table.

segments.name: Metals recycling
segments.note: Collecting and processing scrap metal, which both feeds the company's own mills and is sold to others.

segments.name: Aluminum
segments.note: The new aluminum flat-rolled products mill, still ramping up — sales rose from just $71M a year ago as production started.

segments.name: Steel fabrication
segments.note: Steel joists and deck for construction — shipments rose 18% from the prior quarter and the order backlog is 50% higher than a year ago.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Selling, general and administrative costs of running the company.

opex.name: Profit sharing
opex.note: Profit-sharing payments to employees, which rise and fall with the company's earnings.

opex.name: Amortization
opex.note: Amortization of intangible assets from past acquisitions — a non-cash charge.

takeaways.title: Record shipments meet better prices
takeaways.text: Steel operations shipped a record 3.8 million tons at $1,400 per ton while scrap costs eased, lifting steel operating income 43% from the prior quarter to $1,033M.

takeaways.title: Aluminum is becoming real revenue
takeaways.text: Aluminum sales jumped from $71M to $476M as the new flat-rolled mill ramped up. It still lost $26M in the quarter on startup costs, though it was breakeven before depreciation.

takeaways.title: Cash funds buybacks and growth
takeaways.text: Operations generated $846M of cash; the company spent $150M on capital projects, paid $76M of dividends and repurchased $276M of its own shares, keeping $2.4B of liquidity.

oneTimers: Aluminum operations recorded a $26M operating loss in the quarter from startup and ramp-up costs at the new mill — an improvement from a $33M loss in the prior quarter.
